description: the inline string compare is restored in slot 4: the gate decides the tenant again instead of asking the owner (D-9, C11:4723). Build-killed: no behaviour differs on any input a conformant build can produce, which is why the fence is at the source.

slot 4 asserts the REQUEST's own tenant instead of the record's — a call that cannot fail, and a gate that looks enforced and is not. Live-killed on N4: with the tenant filter and slot 3 neutralised, tenant A's submission of tenant B's record reaches slot 4, passes it, and stops past 4.
the owner's raise is swallowed and slot 4 passes: `tenant_mismatch` becomes unreachable. Live-killed on N4, at both entry levels; the [HTTP] kill is the E-INDEP evidence for G4-b (§3.2 Gate 4).

IR4-7: the gateway drops the port argument, so slot 4 stops running on the bound TENANT_SCOPE. With IR4-3 applied there is no interim default left, so this is a compile break — which is the point: the wiring cannot be lost silently.
